title: Partner Co-sell / Pipeline Review - Acme Corp
summary: Partner co-sell pipeline review focused on three joint opportunities, alignment on qualification, next steps for joint exec briefing and technical POC, discussion of pricing credits and territory motion.
transcript:
Header: 2025-02-25 16:00 UTC / Duration ~45m / Attendees: Maya, Evan (Redwood); Tom, Nina, Rahul (Acme)

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can everyone hear me ok?
00:04 - Tom: Yep, sounds good.
00:06 - Nina: Good here.
00:08 - Maya: Great. Quick agenda — run through the joint pipeline, call out any blockers, decide POC owners and timeline, and sync on partner credits.
00:15 - Rahul: Works for me.
00:18 - Evan: I'll jump in on the technical asks as we go.
00:22 - Tom: So I'll start with deal one — RetailCo RFP. We're in final eval, they've got throughput and latency questions and their security team asked about private deployment options.
00:32 - Maya: Cool. RetailCo — is that an inbound lead that Acme introduced, or co-sourced?
00:36 - Tom: Co-sourced, Acme introduced them last September, we did initial demo in January. They're sensitive on PII and want either dedicated or private.
00:45 - Evan: Understood. From a technical standpoint, the main ask is VPC/private deployment and SOC2 plus KMS integration, right?
00:52 - Rahul: Exactly. Also they mentioned token-level cost concerns; they asked about batching knobs and quantization recommendations.
00:59 - Maya: We can cover both. For private we can do a VPC control plane and on-prem package — that's available. I'll share the security pack, but the SOC2 artifact and KMS integration notes are in the doc we shared — link in the deck: https://redwood.example.com/docs/security-pack (note: link is shorthand).
01:15 - Tom: Great. On pricing, RetailCo wants a committed price for predictable monthly spend. How do we typically structure that for Dedicated?
01:22 - Maya: For Dedicated we do reserved capacity commitments — monthly or annual — and we can tier credits for co-sell partners. For RetailCo, if Acme signs the referral then we normally provide a co-sell credit of 10-20% depending on ARR and commit length.
01:34 - Nina: Is that discount pre-negotiated or do we need a deal desk approval?
01:38 - Maya: For the numbers above it's standard but anything beyond 20% or non-standard contract terms goes to deal desk. We can pre-clear a 15% credit for this opportunity if you can get us a rough ARR estimate.
01:47 - Tom: I'll follow up with ARR estimates after this call.
01:50 - Evan: On the latency/cost tradeoff — our recommended approach for RetailCo is Dedicated with prefix caching and a moderate quantization profile to save tokens, plus request routing to smaller sequence-length optimized kernels. We should run a short benchmark though.
02:02 - Rahul: Benchmark — what does that look like? Timeframe?
02:05 - Evan: We can do a 48-72 hour run using a 2k-token workload sample. We'll need a representative prompt set and a sample of their concurrency pattern.
02:14 - Tom: We can push that next week if the customer signs an NDA.
02:18 - Maya: Good. Action: Evan to own benchmark, Tom to get NDA and sample prompt set.
02:23 - Nina: noted.
02:25 - 02:30 - (small cross talk)
02:30 - Tom: Deal two — FinServ Bank. This is the larger one, but it's deep into procurement and they asked about data residency (EU only) and audit logs. Also they wanted to know whether we have a model catalog with verified performance profiles.
02:44 - Maya: We do. Our model catalog lists Redwood-verified profiles and perf numbers; I can send the perf sheet for comparable models. For data residency we can deploy in EU-only regions or private box in their DC — depends on timeline.
02:56 - Rahul: Security will want EKM/HSM support for keys, and the bank's compliance team will require 7 years of audit logs in immutable storage.
03:05 - Evan: Audit logs — our console supports long retention but the on-prem option can stream logs to the customer's SIEM. We'll need to confirm retention SLA in the SOW.
03:14 - Tom: Procurement asked about backups and disaster recovery — they want RTO/RPO numbers.
03:18 - Maya: Evan, do we have RTO/RPO guidance for private deployments?
03:22 - Evan: Yes, standard is RTO <4 hours for critical services with dedicated runs, RPO <1 hour depending on replication settings; we can provide doc. But if they require sub-30m RTO that's an advanced offering and we'd need SLA add-on.
03:35 - Tom: I'll flag that with FinServ and get back.\03:38 - Maya: Ok. For the co-sell motion — who owns exec briefing and who's on the walk-through?
03:42 - Tom: Acme will lead the business exec outreach — they have an account exec. Redwood should lead a tech exec briefing: Maya + Evan.
03:49 - Maya: Works. We'll plan a joint exec call next week pending NDA.
03:53 - Nina: Deal three quick hit — LogisticsCo PoC. It's a faster cycle, they want a 2-week POC to prove latency and throughput, small budget.
04:02 - Maya: That's ideal — quick POC, focused scope. We recommend hosted API with dedicated pool burst to reduce setup time; if they need private later we can transition.
04:12 - Rahul: Their infra team is small — they'd prefer hosted to avoid ops.
04:15 - Evan: For a 2-week POC we can allocate a small dedicated pool and run throughput tests. We'll need sample traffic.
04:22 - Tom: Ok. Any blockers on providing a POC credit?
04:25 - Maya: For partner-sourced POCs we typically provide a 30-60 day trial credit; I can raise a POC credit request after we get an MoU.
04:33 - Nina: Perfect.
04:35 - (15s pause)
04:50 - Tom: A couple of open items — attribution on logos and joint marketing motion. Acme wants to co-brand an announcement if we win RetailCo.
04:59 - Maya: We're open to co-marketing; legal will need to sign off on logo usage. I'll loop in marketing and legal. We'll share a short co-marketing template: https://redwood.example.com/partner/co-marketing-template
05:12 - Rahul: Also a technical question — latency SLA for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated. What's the number we can promise?
05:18 - Evan: Hosted is best-effort; typical p95 for hosted small seq is 200-400ms depending on model. Dedicated SLA is p95 < 250ms for configured capacity, with SLOs in contract. Important to align on model size — larger models have higher latencies.
05:33 - Tom: The customer specifically called out a 150ms p95 target for a 1k token average, is that realistic?
05:40 - Evan: 150ms at 1k tokens is aggressive for most open models unless you use optimized kernels and smaller models or heavy batching; could be possible with quantized model and pinned inference on high-end GPUs but that's an advanced setup and cost will reflect that.
05:55 - Maya: This is a typical push-pull on latency vs cost. We'll need to surface that tradeoff to the buyer.
06:00 - Nina: For the joint exec — would it help to present benchmark tradeoff graphs?
06:05 - Evan: Yes. I'll produce a simple chart showing latency vs cost across model variants and quant levels.
06:10 - Tom: Great.
06:12 - Maya: Let's capture owners and next steps.
06:15 - Evan: Owner: Benchmark for RetailCo — Evan. Deliverable: 48-72h perf run and chart. Due: 2025-03-03.
06:24 - Tom: Owner: NDA and prompt set — Tom (Acme). Due: 2025-02-28.
06:29 - Maya: Owner: Co-sell credit request — Maya to submit to deal desk. Due: 2025-02-27.
06:34 - Nina: Owner: Joint exec scheduling — Nina. Due: 2025-02-26.
06:39 - Tom: Also, I'll add RetailCo and FinServ into our joint pipeline sheet — sharing link in chat.
06:44 - Maya: Thanks. We'll also send the security pack and perf sheet after the call.
06:49 - Rahul: A quick note — FinServ asked about third-party model governance. How do you handle model updates and drift detection?
06:56 - Evan: We have model versioning and rollout support, and Redwood Optimize has regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets; we can include that in the SOW and show the eval dashboard during the exec.
07:06 - Tom: Excellent.
07:09 - (wrap up)
07:12 - Maya: Any other questions?
07:13 - Tom: None here.
07:14 - Nina: All good.
07:15 - Maya: Ok recap: Evan runs benchmark, Tom provides NDA and prompts, Maya files credit request, Nina schedules exec. We'll follow up with security pack, perf sheet, and joint pipeline doc. Thanks everyone.
07:30 - Tom: Thanks, bye.
07:32 - Maya: Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and auto-transcription errors expected (e.g., 'EKM' sometimes transcribed as 'EKM' vs 'HSM', 'quantization' sometimes 'quantisation').
next_steps: Evan to run 48-72h benchmark for RetailCo and share latency vs cost chart by 2025-03-03
Tom to secure NDA and provide sample prompt set by 2025-02-28
Maya to submit partner co-sell credit request to deal desk by 2025-02-27
Nina to schedule joint exec briefing next week by 2025-02-26
Maya to share security pack and perf sheet after call
action_items: Evan: Benchmark run and chart - due 2025-03-03
Maya: Submit co-sell credit request - due 2025-02-27
Maya: Share security pack & perf sheet - no later than 2025-02-26
